pensamiento:
I'm checking the BAN-12 user story against the quality criteria. It reads as well-formed, and it covers a single requirement, hiding account balances, with no extra notes or parentheses. QUS-004 is where I'm pausing now.

Now I'm going through the INV criteria, and most of them check out. For INV-005, the point about "versiones que soporta la app" seems vague, since the supported versions aren't defined, though the offline and accessible-label checks are observable.

Next I'm checking the DOR criteria, starting with dependencies: hiding balances looks like a local UI change, since the balances already appear on screen, so I don't see a new integration to flag. The business rules seem explicit enough, with the offline case covered, and the non-functional requirements don't apply here because the feature isn't critical or high-volume.

I'm checking whether the BAN-12 authentication criterion applies here. Hiding and showing balances isn't a sensitive operation like a transfer or a device change, and the balances are already visible on the main screen today, so revealing them after the session is authenticated doesn't weaken anything.

I'm weighing whether BM-002 applies, since the criterion mentions the session but never says when it expires or what happens when the app is reopened. The toggle's saved state and the reveal without reauthentication both depend on that session, so I'm checking whether the story actually touches session handling.

I'm weighing whether BM-002 applies to this story, since the text mentions "sesión activa" to permit reveal without reauthentication but never says when that session expires. I'm inclined to flag it as a gap, though I want to be sure the text actually shows it and that I'm not flagging on instinct.

I'm leaning toward flagging BM-002 as a mayor defect, since revealing balances without reauthentication depends on a session lifetime the story never defines. I'd want the analyst to say how long the session lasts, for example after inactivity, before I decide whether to return the story. Next I'm moving on to BM-003, the masking of sensitive data.

I'm checking whether masking applies beyond the screen, since balances can also show up in notifications and logs. The story shows the hidden state as "••••••", but it doesn't say whether that masking carries into those other places, so I'll note that as an open question.

I'm checking BM-004 next: the preference is stored on the device, but it's just a non-sensitive on/off flag, not credentials, so it doesn't conflict with the storage controls and I'll mark it as met. BM-005 doesn't apply because the story doesn't change any monetary operation or modify data. For BM-006 I'm looking at accessibility, since the story mentions an accessible label for the toggle.

Next I'm finishing the BM checks: TalkBack support is covered, and the offline case already handles the loading gap in BM-007, so I'll mark it as met. For BM-008 the story names both platforms and defers the supported versions to the app's existing configuration, so I'm inclined to mark it met as well.

I'm checking BM-009 against the Ley 8968 data rules: the preference is only an on/off flag stored on the device, so no new personal data is collected and I'll mark it as met. For BM-010 I'm weighing whether hiding the balances counts as changing the information given to the client, since the criterion is about financial information and this toggle is the client's own display choice; I'm leaning toward not applicable, but I'd want Cumplimiento to confirm that.

I'm weighing whether BM-002 really applies here: the session is only mentioned in the reveal condition, and I'd need to see whether the story affects session handling. Hiding balances on the home screen looks like a UI preference, and since the balance is still reachable by tapping, I don't think it reduces the information the client must receive, so BM-010 is not applicable.
